_comments: You are reviewing and updating the VAT/tax profile for one country. Please treat the following as the review brief. The full technical and data specification is available in countries/README.md. This data powers Global VAT Help, a reference tool used by tax professionals. Accuracy and reliability are therefore more important than speed or completeness based on assumptions.

If any requirement, tax treatment, rate, threshold, or other value is ambiguous or cannot be verified with sufficient confidence, do not guess or infer the answer. Instead, flag the issue and ask the maintainer a specific question. Never provide or approve a rate, threshold, tax rule, or interpretation that cannot be supported by a reliable source.
Review and edit ONLY the assigned country file. review.md and generated.json located beside it are generated files and must be treated as read-only. Do not modify them.

Verify country.std as the country's standard VAT/tax rate expressed as a percentage. Verify country.reduced as all applicable reduced VAT/tax rates expressed as percentages and listed in descending order. Verify reducedCategories as the goods and services to which each reduced rate applies. Every rate referenced in reducedCategories must correspond exactly to a rate included in country.reduced.

Verify threshold as the VAT/tax registration threshold applicable specifically to a FOREIGN seller. This is a free-text field and should clearly state the amount and currency, together with any relevant qualification where necessary.

Verify vatPattern as the VAT-number validation regex. This field applies to EU countries only. Verify subRegions as state, province, or other subnational tax rates and use this only for tax systems where rates are determined at state/province or comparable subnational level.

The rules section contains the explanations displayed when THIS country has the right to tax the transaction. Review and, where necessary, rewrite the name and detail fields so that they accurately and clearly explain the applicable tax treatment.
Do not remove, rename, translate, or modify the {{from}}, {{to}}, {{loc}}, or {{buyerRate}} placeholders. They are dynamically substituted by the application.

Do NOT change country.code. It must always correspond exactly to the country folder name. The eu and system fields affect the application's tax determination logic. Change these fields ONLY if you have verified that the existing value is genuinely incorrect.

Verify zeroRates as the codes this country's sellers must put on a 0% / exempt invoice. `system` and `field` name the e-invoicing or reporting regime and the XML element carrying the code. Each entry has `code` (the national code, or the EN 16931 category where there is no national list), `name`, `ref` (the legal provision), `en16931` (the equivalent UNCL5305 category) and `appliesTo` (the rule ids where THIS country is the seller and the code is determined by the relation alone — an empty list means the code depends on seller status or on what is being sold, which the calculator does not ask). Set zeroRates.verified to true only once the list is checked against the official specification.

All material tax information must be checked against reliable and up-to-date sources. Official and primary sources should be used wherever available, including national tax authorities, ministries of finance, official government legislation databases, EU institutions and official EU tax resources, and other competent public authorities.
Secondary sources may be used for interpretation or cross-checking, but they should not replace an available authoritative primary source for key tax rates, thresholds, or rules.

Once the country's data has been fully reviewed and verified, set meta.status to "reviewed", fill in meta.reviewedBy and meta.reviewedAt, and add the authoritative sources used during the review to meta.sources.
Only mark the profile as "reviewed" when the relevant information has actually been checked and any material uncertainty has been resolved or explicitly raised with the maintainer.

P-B2B-3-3.name: Cross-border goods — destination country
P-B2B-3-3.detail: Taxed under the destination country's ({{to}}) rules.

P-B2B-EU-3.name: Export of goods — 0%
P-B2B-EU-3.detail: Exempt export from {{from}}. Import VAT and customs duty are collected by {{to}} (consignments ≤ €150: by the seller via IOSS).

P-B2B-STAY.name: Domestic sale — the goods do not leave the country
P-B2B-STAY.detail: The goods do not physically move to another country, so it is a domestic sale within {{from}}. The foreign buyer pays the seller's domestic VAT and can typically reclaim it via a VAT refund.

P-B2C-3-3.name: B2C goods — place of purchase
P-B2C-3-3.detail: The consumer is taxed at the place of purchase ({{from}}).

P-B2C-STAY.name: B2C purchase in the seller's country — the goods do not leave
P-B2C-STAY.detail: The buyer purchases locally (or carries the goods away themselves), so it is a domestic sale in the seller's country ({{from}}): {{from}}'s rate applies and the distance-selling threshold is irrelevant.

P-DOM-B2B.name: Domestic sale (B2B)
P-DOM-B2B.detail: Ordinary domestic sale of goods, taxed by {{to}}.

P-DOM-B2C.name: Domestic sale (B2C)
P-DOM-B2C.detail: Ordinary domestic sale of goods, taxed by {{to}}.

S-B2B-3-X-RC.name: Service export — per the seller's country (typically 0%)
S-B2B-3-X-RC.detail: The seller invoices under their own country's ({{from}}) export rule: B2B services to non-resident businesses are 0% / GST-free in most countries — but that is decided by {{from}}, not {{to}}. On the buyer's side ({{to}}), ~{{buyerRate}}% arises via reverse charge.

S-B2B-EU-3.name: B2B service — outside EU VAT
S-B2B-EU-3.detail: The place of supply is {{to}} (outside the EU). No EU VAT; the buyer follows local rules.

S-B2C-DIG-3-3.name: Digital service (B2C) — destination
S-B2C-DIG-3-3.detail: Taxed under the destination country's ({{to}}) digital rules.

S-B2C-DIG-EU-3.name: Digital service (B2C) — outside EU VAT
S-B2C-DIG-EU-3.detail: 0% EU VAT; the place of supply is {{to}}, under the destination country's digital rules (registration may be required there).

S-B2C-GEN-3.name: B2C service — supplier's country (local)
S-B2C-GEN-3.detail: The place of supply is the foreign supplier's country ({{from}}); no EU VAT.

S-ONSITE.name: Location-bound service — by place of performance
S-ONSITE.detail: Real-estate-related / event admission / restaurant / on-site service: taxed where it physically takes place ({{loc}}) — even for B2B, with no reverse charge. Local tax registration is typically required.
